component.name: ATO20
component.summary: Tabletop RPG scenes on your TV

description.p: ATO20 runs the visual side of a tabletop RPG session played around a real table. You build the next scene on your laptop while the table keeps watching the current one on the TV, and each player follows their own character sheet on their phone.

A campaign is a folder on your disk, like a vault in Obsidian. Maps, portraits, handouts, notes and audio live in it as ordinary files, so you can back it up, sync it or move it to another machine without exporting anything.

Scenes hold maps with tokens, hidden areas, saved camera framings and measuring tools. Boards are scenes without a floor, for planning: free text, arrows that stay anchored to what you move, sticky notes and live Markdown cards. What the table sees is whatever you choose to put on air.
Everything runs on your own machine. The phones and the TV reach it over the local network, so a session works with no internet connection and without an account.

description.p: On Windows, the installer file now shows the ATO20 icon too. Version 0.1.3 fixed the installed app and its shortcut, but the downloaded setup.exe still showed the packaging tool's generic globe.
Packages now ship the ATO20 icon: the tent with a d20 on a dark tile. Until now every build carried the packaging toolkit's default icon.
Fixes the store page announcing the previous version's changes. Behind the scenes only: nothing changes for people running the AppImage or the Windows installer.

Groundwork for the Linux stores. Nothing changes in the app itself: fonts are no longer downloaded while packaging, and the update notice steps aside in store builds, where the store is what updates you.

First beta. Campaigns gain boards: a floorless sheet with free text, anchored arrows and live Markdown cards. Files, notes and images now share one folder tree, dice can be rolled by notation, the ruler became a measuring shape placed on the map, and the bookshelf shows covers.
